items.title: Dana-Farber + 23andMe: rare genetic risk factor for lung cancer in never-smokers (EGFR)
bullets: @DanaFarber (Following): @DFarberThoracic research with @23andMe identified a rare genetic risk factor for lung cancer in people who have never smoked.

Framed as potentially shaping future screening strategies for carriers of the EGFR-related risk; NYT coverage circulating with the post (“This Rare Gene Drastically Raises Lung Cancer Risk in People Who Never Smoked”).
Clearest fresh solid-tumor genetics beat overnight — distinct from yesterday’s bladder VOLGA Priority Review.
items.need_to_know: Top cancer overnight: Dana-Farber/23andMe rare genetic risk linked to lung cancer in never-smokers, with EGFR-carrier screening implications.

items.title: Etentamig Phase III CERVINO: BCMA/CD3 bispecific beats SOC in triple-class-exposed RRMM
bullets: @CancerNetwrk (Following): etentamig improved responses and PFS vs standard therapies in triple-class-exposed relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
Novel BCMA/CD3 bispecific met both co-primary endpoints of Phase III CERVINO; early overall-survival trend noted in the write-up.
Strongest hematologic Phase III readout overnight alongside LINKER-SMM1 smoldering-myeloma signal (also_noted).
items.need_to_know: Myeloma beat: Phase III CERVINO — etentamig (BCMA/CD3) superior to SOC on responses/PFS in heavily pretreated RRMM.

items.title: Nectin-4 RNA as EV biomarker: ORR/OS link in 1L EV+pembrolizumab (not pembro alone)
bullets: @scocmem / OncoAlert circuit (Brain): more evidence for Nectin-4 as a biomarker for enfortumab vedotin — European Urology.
In first-line EV+pembrolizumab, high Nectin-4 RNA expression associated with ORR and OS; association not seen with pembrolizumab alone.
Biomarker follow-on to yesterday’s VOLGA Priority Review headline — selection biology, not another regulatory label.
items.need_to_know: Bladder/EV biomarker: high Nectin-4 RNA tied to outcomes with EV+PD-1 but not PD-1 alone.

items.title: Norwitz on Cell: “attention problems” may be sleep / arousal–reward problems
bullets: @nicknorwitz (Following + Brain): thread on new Cell research — what we call attention problems may be sleep problems wearing a disguise.
Stimulants (Ritalin/Vyvanse) long assumed to turn up “attention”; imaging/biology framing lights arousal and reward systems instead — helps resolve stimulant paradoxes.
Practical close: for many, fix sleep/dopamine context before assuming pure attention deficit; StayCuriousMetabolism letter linked.
items.need_to_know: Metabolic/neuro beat: Norwitz highlights Cell work reframing ADHD-like attention issues around sleep and reward circuitry.

items.title: Bikman: Asian descent — “normal” BMI can still mean significant metabolic risk
bullets: @BenBikmanPhD (Following): since an Asia research fellowship, focused on ethnicity × body-weight differences.
Punchline: if you’re of Asian descent, a “normal” BMI can still come with significant metabolic risk — BMI as a blunt instrument across ancestries.
Fresh insulin/IR literacy signal on a still-thin Keto-list overnight (~7 in-window); pairs with ICE/compensation chatter in also_noted.
